outcome: Maternal weight gain below and above target
cohort: Individuals with gestational diabetes who received either risk-prioritised or universal medical nutrition therapy across three distinct cohorts (RP1, RP2, UM).
finding: Risk-prioritised medical nutrition therapy (MNT) was a more efficient service approach for gestational diabetes than universal MNT, with comparable overall pregnancy outcomes and even resulted in fewer small-for-gestational-age (SGA) infants in the risk-prioritised group.
mod_finding: No significant increases were observed in early deliveries, induced deliveries, or emergency caesarean sections in the risk-prioritised MNT cohorts compared to the universal MNT cohort.
